question: GQ-001
subject: the unreachability pattern, mechanised instead of fixed a sixth time
the_pattern: Five times this session I built something and left it unreachable — outbox messages, corpus counts, search indexes, the search CLI, and a gate wired to nothing. Each fixed by hand, after noticing.

what_was_already_covered.scripts: audit-asserted-numbers reports script-unreferenced — checked, every script is reachable
what_was_already_covered.not_covered: the thing all five failures actually were — a PAGE a person is expected to read, with no path to it

the_defect_found_by_looking.what: library.html was linked FROM the observatory and linked nowhere itself
the_defect_found_by_looking.consequence: a reader browsing to the corpus hit a dead end and had to edit the URL by hand
the_defect_found_by_looking.fixed: back-link added; round trip verified in both directions over the tailnet

checks: every page reachable from the index
every page links somewhere — a dead end is half a defect
no link to a missing page
refuses to report clean when there are no pages at all
the_mechanism_worked_this_time: audit-verify-chain FLAGGED audit-reachability.mjs as gate-dropped-from-chain before I wired it in. Last turn I had to notice corpus-integrity.mjs myself; this turn the repo told me. That is the difference between a lesson and a mechanism.
